title: Paloma and the Promise Again
premise: Paloma Adeyemi runs a struggling bakery in a coastal town where Gideon Okonkwo, the marine biologist who once broke her heart, has returned to lead a sea-turtle conservation project threatening her lease. When a community center's anonymous pen-pal program accidentally pairs them as correspondents, each begins confiding in a stranger they believe is someone else — and slowly falls for the honesty that face-to-face pride forbids. As the lease deadline and a corrupt councilman's land grab converge, Paloma must expose the truth about both the project and Gideon's role in it. In the end, she speaks the rehearsed sentence of forgiveness aloud, Gideon chooses loyalty to her over his career, and the bakery becomes the conservation program's home base.
about_author: Jonah Yarrow is the pen name of a former coastal-town journalist who spent five years covering small-town zoning battles before turning to fiction. They write love stories about people who mistake stubbornness for self-protection.

chapters.title: Salt in the Flour
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. She counts down ninety days left on her bakery lease while feeding the town gossip mill free day-old bread. Gideon walks in to buy coffee, and ten years of silence collapses between them. The beat: dread disguised as composure.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Volunteering for the community center's pen-pal program to please his new boss, he receives an anonymous letter that reads suspiciously like someone who hates him. He writes back anyway. The beat: cautious curiosity rekindling an old wound.

chapters.title: Turtle Season
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The conservation project's survey stakes appear on the beach behind her bakery, and the town splits into factions. She vents to her anonymous pen pal about 'a man from ten years ago' without naming him. The beat: relief in confession.

chapters.title: What the Letters Don't Say
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. His correspondent's voice haunts him; he starts rearranging survey routes to pass the bakery. Meanwhile he discovers his project's funding traces to Councilman Voss, who wants the waterfront rezoned. The beat: unease beneath attraction.

chapters.title: Low Tide, High Stakes
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Voss offers to save her lease if she publicly endorses the rezoning. She refuses, then nearly tells Gideon everything at a nesting-site vigil — but sees him shaking hands with Voss instead. The beat: betrayal confirmed by misread evidence.

chapters.title: The Unsent Letter
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Realizing his data is being doctored to support Voss's plan, he drafts a letter exposing it — then learns his pen pal's handwriting matches a flour-dusted note on Paloma's counter. The reveal lands mid-sentence. The beat: vertigo of recognition.

chapters.title: Enemies, Properly Introduced
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Confronted with the truth of their correspondence, they fight in the empty bakery — about the decade-old breakup, the letters, the lease. But anger cracks into honesty, and Gideon admits why he really left. The beat: raw catharsis.

chapters.title: Voss's Ledger
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Together they trace the forged environmental reports to Voss, but going public means Gideon loses his career and Paloma risks Voss burying her lease forever. They choose truth anyway. The beat: alliance becoming devotion.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At the packed council hearing, Gideon presents the real data and names Voss's corruption; Paloma testifies about what the waterfront means to the town. Voss falls, but the vote on her lease hangs until an old friend casts the deciding ballot. The beat: terror turning to triumph.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Rehearsed a Decade
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Lease secured, bakery repurposed as the program's field station, Gideon waits among the flour dust. She finally says the sentence she rehearsed for ten years — 'I forgive you, and I choose you again.' First kiss over cooling racks. The beat: belonging, earned twice.
